Thanks again for the time today, Rebecca - really helpful demo and context on the structured output use cases. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

- Objective: validate model fit for Avery's structured extraction + function-calling flows (JSON output that maps to your downstream API).
- What we delivered: attached prompt set (avery_prompt_set_v2.json) and an initial eval harness that exercises function-calling retries and schema validation.
- Suggested models to run first (tradeoff: quality vs cost):
  - redwood-v1-large (best-effort, higher cost; good at schema compliance)
  - Llama-3-13B-instruct (strong generalization to tricky extractions)
  - Mistral-Instruct-7B (cost-efficient baseline)

Immediate next steps:
1) You run the attached prompt set against the three models above (we included a sample runner in the harness).
2) Share the failing examples / logs (if any) - that will help us tune prompts and fallback parsing.
3) We'll run a focused function-calling stress pass (1000 requests/min pattern you described) to validate retries and KV-cache behavior.

Notes on evals & metrics we recommend tracking: schema_accept_rate, parse_success_rate, avg_token_latency, token_cost_per_1000. We added a benchmark sheet link here: https://redwood-internal.sheets/benchmarks/avery-rdw-7521 (also attached in related_links).

One specific ask: can you provide the canonical JSON schema for the outputs (field types, optional vs required)? If you prefer, paste it directly into a reply or upload to the Drive folder we shared. Having that exact schema lets us run strict validation and automated repair flows.

I'll loop Rishi and Aditya into a follow-up sync focused on function-calling edge cases (schema variance, retries, and deterministic parse strategies). Proposed window: Thu 10-11am PT. Does that work for your team?

Attachments: avery_prompt_set_v2.json (application/json), initial_eval_harness.zip (zip)

Great notes, Rebecca - thanks for the logs. Short answers and a proposed policy we can operationalize: 

1) Retry policy (recommended):
   - For non-idempotent downstream actions, do NOT auto-retry function-side effects. Instead: run a "dry-run"/preview function that only returns the payload, validate schema, then call the real API once.
   - For idempotent ops (or when you can detect duplicates), allow up to 2 automatic retries with a backoff (250ms -> 750ms) driven by the runner.

2) Schema validation + repair ordering (production-safe):
   - Step 1: strict schema validation on returned JSON. If valid -> accept.
   - Step 2: if invalid, attempt automated repair via a constrained, schema-guided prompt (single shot).
   - Step 3: if still invalid, run one retry against the same model with an explicit instruction to return the exact schema (include the schema in the prompt).
   - Step 4: if still failing, fallback to second model (e.g., redwood-v1-large -> Llama-3-13B) with same single-retry logic.

3) Metrics to track for continued tuning: schema_accept_rate (by model), repair_success_rate, end_to_end_success_rate, avg_retry_count, and observed duplicate side-effect rate. We recommend alerting on schema_accept_rate < 95% for critical fields.

4) Implementation notes for your runner:
   - Use function-calling interface where the model returns structured args; keep a strict parser that rejects non-JSON payloads.
   - For deterministic parsing, add a short canonicalizing layer: strip trailing commas, normalize numbers, and run a JSON Schema validator (we recommend Ajv for Node).
   - Keep a small repair prompt template we can iterate on; I'll share our initial template after the sync.
